QF.id: Securities Types Features and Asset Allocation Concepts_44

question.text: A company generates stable and regular profits sufficient to make periodic interest payments. It does not want to dilute its existing promoter ownership. Which form of capital is most suitable for this company?

answer.text: Equity capital through a fresh public issue
Preference share capital with voting rights
Warrant issuance to the general public

explanation.text: The Logic: Per p38, stable profits support taking on debt capital, and reluctance to dilute ownership also points to debt. The company has stable cash flows to service interest and wishes to preserve promoter ownership — debt fits both conditions. The Trap: Fresh equity (B) would dilute promoter ownership. Per p41, preference shares do not offer voting rights, so option C ('preference share capital with voting rights') is internally inconsistent and would also dilute ownership. Per p58, exercised warrants are allotted equity shares — leading to dilution if exercised. Note: Choosing debt over equity signals confidence in stable cash flows and a desire to avoid ownership dilution.
